Subject: FintechCo discovery — post-call notes and next steps

Hi Rajiv / Simran —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our 45m discovery:

- Goal: Reduce real-time fraud decision latency and cut inference costs for scoring models by ~35% while keeping model fidelity.
- Current stack: on-prem model server + nightly batch scoring; interested in moving to a hybrid inference setup (low-latency hosted endpoint for lookup + dedicated for high-throughput scoring).
- Key constraints: PCI scope, data residency (US), SLA expectations (99.9% during market hours), and SOC 2 evidence required for procurement.

Proposed next steps (from our side):
1) Share a short mutual action plan and architecture sketch (attached).
2) Introduce Nikhil (solutions engineer) for a 30m technical deep dive to validate integration points and replay sample workload.
3) If tech looks good, propose a 4-week pilot on Dedicated capacity with a controlled subset of traffic.

Can you confirm that this matches your priorities and whether Simran should be the procurement contact? If yes, what does your preferred timeline look like for a tech deep dive (next week or the week after)?

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx, fintechco-architecture-diagram.pdf
Recording: https://drive.google.com/recording/1a2b3c-fintechco-discovery

Thanks — happy to adjust.

--

Marissa —

Quick notes:
- PCI/data residency: we can run Dedicated in the US region and integrate with their KMS via customer-managed keys; requires a short network checklist (IP allowlist + TLS certs). No architectural blockers.
- Sample replay: if they can provide ~24–48h of representative traffic and the model artifact, we can run a low-cost warmup that demonstrates latency/cost improvements.
- Pilot sizing: recommend starting with 1-2 GPUs (A10/A30 class) and enable prefix caching for hot users; costs look favorable in our bench but I'll prepare a short runbook for the call.

I can join the external deep dive — available Tue/Wed morning PT next week.

— Nikhil
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>

Thanks Marissa —

From a CS/POV perspective:
- Success criteria: (1) <=50ms P95 inference for lookups, (2) <35% unit cost reduction vs current baseline, (3) secure KMS integration and audit logs for first 30 days.
- I'd recommend offering a 2-week pilot validity window and include a standard support playbook (daily check-ins first 3 days, weekly after).
- I'll prepare a short onboarding checklist and a sample runbook to drop into the call if they ask about ramp.

I can join the external call for the first 15–20 minutes to set expectations.

— Naomi
